evidence: src/order/order.controller.ts: create() reads dto.customerId, dto.quantity and dto.unitPrice and calls this.orderService.create(...) without applying any rules itself
src/order/order.controller.ts: findOne() maps @Param('id') straight to this.orderService.findOne(id)
Uses only NestJS transport decorators (@Controller('orders'), @Post(), @Get(':id'), @Body(), @Param()), which is the presentation layer's role
parsedVerdict.reasoning: OrderController sits in the presentation layer and only does transport work. It maps HTTP routes with @Controller, @Post and @Get. It binds the request body and path parameters with @Body and @Param. Then it hands the work to the injected OrderService. It has no business rules (the service gets quantity and unitPrice as they are, with no calculation or validation in the controller), no persistence, and no infrastructure logic. Pulling customerId out of the DTO is just passing parameters along. Returning OrderEntity as the response type means the controller exposes a domain type in its responses. That is about type exposure and dependency direction, which belong to the import and layer-dependency checks that are out of scope here. It is not a misplaced responsibility.
